title: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows
summary: Expert called MAHA's spending "pretty unusual" for a PAC.
body: In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement's midterm wipeout , a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA's own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group's priority was ever winning elections in the first place. The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates. The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA's clout in the midterms . In reality, MAHA PAC took in $3.2 million. During the election cycle, the PAC spent more than $10.5 million, with over $7 million coming from money it had collected previously. title: "الحكام ليسوا الأشرار".. مونويرا يكشف سر الذكاء الاصطناعي في إعادة اللقطات

title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
summary: Lawsuit: Over 99% of school system’s AI gun alerts were false positives.
body: In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed. The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t. Read full article Comments

title: Google turns to Blue Origin for a rocket, but its long-term problem remains
summary: "Project Suncatcher is a long-term moonshot."
body: Blue Origin announced Thursday that its New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029 as part of that company's Project Suncatcher program. Google disclosed it was working on scalable orbiting data centers about a year ago and characterized the project as one of its research "moonshots." The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy. "Project Suncatcher is a long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit," said Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher at Google, in the news release. "This dedicated launch with Blue Origin represents a crucial milestone on our roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what's possible for the future of compute." Read full article Comments

title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
summary: Some models fare better, but all fail in similar ways.
body: Many studies over the years have examined how people encounter climate science information. Some focused on the top results that Google surfaced (back when Google was still in the business of serving links), while others examined social media content or newspaper and TV news coverage. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a share of the public information diet, it's worth looking at how they handle climate change. But there’s no direct way for researchers to look at the information people have seen. It is served ephemerally to individual users, confined to their chat session. A study led by researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) tried to tackle this question from multiple angles, testing LLMs with different prompts and evaluating their output. They started with benchmarks of simple factual questions (benchmarks that might even be in models’ training data at this point) but also analyzed more complex interactions—including when users think they’re right to push back on an answer. title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
summary: Google says almost all developers have already gotten on board with verification.
body: Google announced Android developer verification last year , and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead . It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon. The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure . Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps. In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. body: Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 There's something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it's the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watched other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn't watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature. The team randomly assigned male mice to three groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training with three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them. title: NASA's new Moon plans have a problem: Orion wasn't designed to fly this way
summary: "We also have a responsibility to not go too fast and cut too many corners."
body: NASA recently announced a significant shakeup to the Artemis program that will land humans on the Moon. The moves were designed to give the agency's lunar lander providers—SpaceX with its Starship vehicle, and Blue Origin with Blue Moon—more flexibility in reaching the Moon. For Starship, this means docking with Orion in Earth orbit, and then traveling to the Moon in tandem. For Blue Moon, it shifts the rendezvous with Orion all the way to low-lunar orbit. These changes benefit the lunar landers, but in turn impose more of a burden on the Orion spacecraft, which is built for NASA by Lockheed Martin. Across just four consecutive business days, a mass Microsoft exchange outage broke IT services for thousands of companies , a Federal Aviation Administration tech screw-up grounded airplanes across the country, a software problem affecting JPMorgan Chase caused another round of disruption, a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights yet again, and an NSA classified network’s downtime left the agency’s staff sitting at home waiting to return to their office at Fort Meade. In the midst of a US war with Iran and rising fears of AI-enabled hacking , this still-unfolding comedy of IT errors colliding across American infrastructure felt to plenty of observers like more than a coincidence. title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
summary: Hardened defaults align with DoD standards, but there may be growing pains.
body: Microsoft's Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core . Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency's (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: "The s ecure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened. " The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance. body: The computer gaming world hasn't heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity , The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright's subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA . Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players' memories. MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright's previous projects by "turn[ing] the simulation inward," as Wright's Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world. “If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?"
